t: Section 5305(g) of title 49, United States Code, is amended by striking “2011 and for the period beginning on October 1, 2011, and ending on June 30, 2012” and inserting “2012”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that replaces a date range in an existing code provision. The tempting reading is that 49 U.S.C. 5305 concerns transportation planning, which may involve states or the public elsewhere, but nothing in this text creates or requires consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision here.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute that changes a date range. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative housekeeping provision.
qwen_block.s: Section 5305(g) of title 49, United States Code, is amended by striking “2011 and for the period beginning on October 1, 2011, and ending on June 30, 2012” and inserting “2012”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that only changes the dates in a funding-availability provision of 49 U.S.C. 5305(g). It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. It is tempting to say Yes because section 5305 deals with transit planning that involves States and metropolitan planning organizations, but nothing in this text involves those outside parties.
opus.s: is amended by striking “2011 and for the period beginning on October 1, 2011, and ending on June 30, 2012” and inserting “2012”
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** You might be tempted to say "Yes" because 49 U.S.C. § 5305 is the transit planning section, and transit planning involves metropolitan planning organizations and States, which are outside the federal government. That reading doesn't hold up. This amendment only swaps one date range for another ("2012") in subsection (g), which deals with when funds are available. The text itself sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
